help.wsHelp: Define how this WebSocket endpoint behaves. Add messages to send on connect, in response to incoming messages (by pattern matching), or periodically.
help.proxyTransformHelp: Change the request before it reaches the backend and the response before it goes back, the way a BFF would. Rules are applied first and the script afterwards, so the script has the final say.
help.proxyRecordingHelp: Saves every backend response as a mock route. They are created inactive on purpose: an active mock shadows this proxy and there would be nothing left to record. Activate them when the session is done.
help.faultsHelp: Makes the route slow, unreliable, or both. This is what you need to test timeouts, retries and degradation, which a mock that always answers instantly cannot exercise. On a proxy route the delay happens before calling the backend, and an injected fault never reaches it.
help.templatingDesc: Replaces {{...}} in the body and headers with request data or generated values. Off by default, because a response can legitimately contain {{...}}.
help.sequenceHelp: Makes the route answer differently depending on how many times it has been called: first pending, then processing, then done. This is what simulates a polling flow, which conditions cannot: they only look at the request, and in a poll every request is identical. The step wins over conditions. The counter lives in memory and resets when the server restarts.
help.mockScriptHelp: Transforms the response with JavaScript before sending it. It runs last: it sees the final body, after conditions, the scenario and templating. It can read the request with ms.request.json() and change the response with ms.response.code, ms.response.headers and ms.response.setBody().

mcp.intro: Create a connection so an AI assistant can list, create and edit routes for you. Generate a token, copy the command and paste it into your terminal.

mcp.securityBody: The token grants permission to create, modify and delete routes. Treat it like a password and revoke it when it is no longer needed.

help.name: It is only there to recognise the connection later; create one per machine or per assistant.
help.command: Paste it as is into your terminal. The URL comes from the address you used to open this panel.

mcp.hintGeneric: Any client that speaks MCP over HTTP needs this URL and this header.

notes.vscode: It has to go in .vscode/mcp.json. In a .mcp.json at the project root, VS Code silently drops the headers and the connection fails for lack of authentication.
notes.claudeDesktop: Claude Desktop does not speak MCP over HTTP directly: the command uses mcp-remote as a bridge, so it needs Node installed. On Windows there is a known bug escaping spaces in the arguments.
notes.codex: Codex reads the token from an environment variable, not from the file. Export MOCK_SERVER_TOKEN before starting it.
